evidence_entailment_note: Computed over accepted items, as at G1. Group-level flags reported by the verifiers were {'a': 'FAIL', 'b': 'FAIL', 'c': 'PASS'}; every one is driven by an item this wave rejected, and each is recorded as that item's rejection reason rather than as a breach of an accepted-item invariant.

COMPETITOR_WITHOUT_STEM_ANCHOR.diagnosis: This is the surviving G1 mode, and G2 supplies its cause. A competitor's frozen correctness condition names the stem feature under which it would be right, so the natural way to write a stem that keeps the key unique is to report that feature absent. Doing so removes the positive pull the competitor needed, and the option becomes one nothing in the stem invites. No automated gate covers it: ADM-3 catches only a negation that defeats exactly one competitor and grounds nothing in the key, so a stem that negates every competitor passes ADM-3 and still produces an anchorless set.

KEY_DISTRACTOR_REGISTER_ASYMMETRY.diagnosis: Created by the provenance rule itself. Distractor text is locked to the curated competitor concept string so that it cannot be authored freehand, while the key is written fresh for the item. The key then differs in grammatical form, hedging and length from every distractor. ADM-5 measures numerals and paired quantities only, so it does not see this.

OPTION_NESTING_BETWEEN_KEY_AND_A_RETRIEV.diagnosis: Retrieval returned a competitor that properly contains the key: digitally delivered cognitive behavioural therapy is an instance of structured psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy. Retrieval excludes a competitor whose correctness conditions are fully satisfied, which catches a second key, and has no test for a competitor that subsumes the key.

RATIONALE_CLAIM_OUTSIDE_THE_ITEM_EVIDENC.diagnosis: A rationale asserts something true of the topic and present in the packet, but not in the claim set this item declared. The critical-fact layer adjudicates declared claims and nothing checks that a rationale stays inside them.
